Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
The first published sketch, "A Dinner at Poplar Walk" brought tears to Dickens's eyes when he discovered it in the pages of The Monthly Magazine. From then on his sketches, which appeared under the pen name "Boz" in The Evening Chronicle, earned him a modest reputation.
第一篇发表的速写《波普拉散步道之宴》，当狄更斯在《月刊》上发现它时，曾令他热泪盈眶。此后，他以"博兹"为笔名在《晚宪报》上发表的速写，为他赢得了一份不大却实在的声名。
B
The runaway success of The Pickwick Papers, as it is generally known today, secured Dickens's fame. There were Pickwick coats and Pickwick cigars, and the plump, spectacled hero, Samuel Pickwick, became a national figure.
正如今天人们所熟知的那样，《匹克威克外传》的一炮而红奠定了狄更斯的名声。市面上出现了匹克威克外套和匹克威克雪茄，而那位肥胖戴镜的主人公塞缪尔·匹克威克成了全国知名人物。
C
Soon after Sketches by Boz appeared, a publishing firm approached Dickens to write a story in monthly installments, as a backdrop for a series of woodcuts by the then-famous artist Robert Seymour, who had originated the idea for the story. With characteristic confidence, Dickens successfully insisted that Seymour's pictures illustrate his own story instead. After the first installment, Dickens wrote to the artist and asked him to correct a drawing Dickens felt was not faithful enough to his prose. Seymour made the change, went into his backyard, and expressed his displeasure by committing suicide. Dickens and his publishers simply pressed on with a new artist. The comic novel, The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club, appeared serially in 1836 and 1837, and was first published in book form in 1837.
《博兹速写集》问世后不久，一家出版公司找上狄更斯，请他按月连载一篇故事，作为当时著名画家罗伯特·西摩所创想的一系列木刻的陪衬。狄更斯以一贯的自信，成功坚持要西摩的画来图解他自己的故事。第一期的插图登出后，狄更斯写信给画家，请他修改一幅他觉得不够忠实于自己散文的画。西摩改了画，走进后院，以自杀表达了他的不快。狄更斯和出版商则换了个新画家继续干。这部喜剧小说《匹克威克俱乐部遗稿》于1836和1837年连载，并于1837年首次以书籍形式出版。
D
Charles Dickens is probably the best-known and, to many people, the greatest English novelist of the 19th century. A moralist, satirist, and social reformer. Dickens crafted complex plots and striking characters that capture the panorama of English society.
查尔斯·狄更斯很可能是19世纪最知名、对许多人而言也是最伟大的英国小说家。作为道德家、讽刺家和社会改革者，狄更斯构筑了复杂的情节与鲜明的人物，捕捉了英国社会的全景。
E
Soon after his father's release from prison, Dickens got a better job as errand boy in law offices. He taught himself shorthand to get an even better job later as a court stenographer and as a reporter in Parliament. At the same time, Dickens, who had a reporter's eye for transcribing the life around him especially anything comic or odd, submitted short sketches to obscure magazines.
父亲出狱后不久，狄更斯谋得一份更好的差事——在律师事务所当跑腿小弟。他自学速记，以便日后谋得更好的工作：法庭书记员和议会记者。与此同时，狄更斯有着记者般善于记录周遭生活（尤其是任何滑稽或古怪之事）的眼光，向一些无名杂志投寄短篇速写。
F
Dickens was born in Portsmouth, on England's southern coast. His father was a clerk in the British navy pay office—a respectable position, but with little social status. His paternal grandparents, a steward and a housekeeper possessed even less status, having been servants, and Dickens later concealed their background. Dickens's mother supposedly came from a more respectable family. Yet two years before Dickens's birth, his mother's father was caught stealing and fled to Europe, never to return. The family's increasing poverty forced Dickens out of school at age 12 to work in Warren's Blacking Warehouse, a shoe-polish factory, where the other working boys mocked him as "the young gentleman." His father was then imprisoned for debt. The humiliations of his father's imprisonment and his labor in the blacking factory formed Dickens's greatest wound and became his deepest secret. He could not confide them even to his wife, although they provide the unacknowledged foundation of his fiction.
狄更斯出生于英格兰南部海岸的朴茨茅斯。其父是英国海军薪金处的办事员——地位体面，却少有社会声望。他的祖父母，一位管家与一位女管家，因曾为仆人而身份更低，狄更斯后来隐瞒了他们的背景。狄更斯的母亲据称出自一个更体面的家庭。然而在狄更斯出生前两年，他的外祖父因盗窃被捕并逃往欧洲，再未归来。家境日窘，迫使12岁的狄更斯辍学，到沃伦鞋油厂——一家鞋油工厂——做工，其他童工嘲弄他为"小绅士"。其父随后因债务入狱。父亲入狱的屈辱与在鞋油厂的劳作，构成了狄更斯最大的伤口，也成为他最深的秘密。即便对妻子他也无法吐露，尽管这一切正是其小说不宣的底色。
G
After Pickwick, Dickens plunged into a bleaker world. In Oliver Twist, he traces an orphan's progress from the workhouse to the criminal slums of London. Nicholas Nickleby, his next novel, combines the darkness of Oliver Twist with the sunlight of Pickwick. The popularity of these novels consolidated Dickens as a nationally and internationally celebrated man of letters.
继《匹克威克》之后，狄更斯一头扎进了一个更为黯淡的世界。在《雾都孤儿》中，他追述了一个孤儿从济贫院走向伦敦犯罪贫民窟的历程。他的下一部小说《尼古拉斯·尼克尔贝》将《雾都孤儿》的黑暗与《匹克威克》的明快融为一体。这些小说的走红，巩固了狄更斯作为全国乃至国际知名文坛巨匠的地位。

参考范文

The cartoon presents a thought-provoking contrast. In the left picture, a man reclines before a huge bookshelf, proudly boasting, "I have so many books!"; in the right picture, the same man sits at a desk with one open book, determined to "finish twenty books this year." The caption reads: "Having books" versus "Reading books."

The drawing conveys a clear message: merely possessing resources is not the same as putting them to use. Many people accumulate books, degrees or opportunities as a source of pride, yet never apply them in any meaningful way. A library on the shelf earns no respect; only the act of reading, reflecting and applying what one learns brings real growth. This principle holds true not only for reading but for every sphere of life—from physical exercise to professional skills.

From my perspective, we should resist the vanity of "having" and embrace the discipline of "doing." A single book read thoroughly is far more valuable than a thousand volumes left untouched. Let us set concrete goals, follow them through, and turn what we have into what we actually do.

【译文】

漫画呈现了一组发人深省的对比。左图中，一人斜倚在巨大的书架前，得意地说"我有这么多书！"；右图中，同一个人坐在书桌前，摊开一本书，决心"今年读完20本"。图题为："有书"与"读书"。

这幅画传达了一个清晰的道理：仅仅拥有资源，并不等于加以运用。许多人把书、学位或机会当作骄傲的资本，却从不加以真正利用。书架上的藏书不会赢得尊重；唯有阅读、思考并践行所学，才能带来真正的成长。这一原则不仅适用于读书，也适用于生活的方方面面——从锻炼身体到职业技能。

在我看来，我们应抵制"拥有"的虚荣，拥抱"行动"的自律。一本读透的书，远胜千卷束之高阁的藏书。让我们设定具体目标、贯彻始终，把"所有"变为"所为"。

In a rare unanimous ruling, the US Supreme Court has overturned the corruption conviction of a former Virginia governor, Robert McDonnell. But it did so while holding its nose at the ethics of his conduct, which included accepting gifts such as a Rolex watch and a Ferrari automobile from a company seeking access to government.

在一项罕见的一致裁决中，美国最高法院推翻了对前弗吉尼亚州州长罗伯特·麦克唐纳的腐败定罪。但它在这样做的同时，也对其行为的伦理表示嗤之以鼻——他曾从一家寻求接触政府的公司收受劳力士手表、法拉利汽车等礼物。

The high court's decision said the judge in Mr. McDonnell's trial failed to tell a jury that it must look only at his "official acts," or the former governor's decisions on "specific" and "unsettled" issues related to his duties.

高等法院的裁决说，麦克唐纳案审判中的法官未能告诉陪审团，必须只审视他的"公务行为"，即前州长在与职责相关的"具体"和"未决"问题上的决定。

Merely helping a gift-giver gain access to other officials, unless done with clear intent to pressure those officials, is not corruption, the justices found.

大法官们认定，仅仅帮助送礼者接触其他官员，除非带有明确向那些官员施压的意图，否则不构成腐败。

The court did suggest that accepting favors in return for opening doors is "distasteful" and "nasty." But under anti-bribery laws, proof must be made of concrete benefits, such as approval of a contract or regulation. Simply arranging a meeting, making a phone call, or hosting an event is not an "official act."

The court's ruling is legally sound in defining a kind of favoritism that is not criminal. Elected leaders must be allowed to help supporters deal with bureaucratic problems without fear of prosecution of bribery. "The basic compact underlying representative government," wrote Chief Justice John Roberts for the court, "assumes that public officials will hear from their constituents and act on their concerns."

该裁决在法律上合理地界定了一种不构成犯罪的偏袒行为。民选领导人必须被允许帮助支持者处理官僚问题，而无需担忧被诉贿赂。首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨代表法院写道："代议制政府背后的基本契约，假定公职人员会听取选民的意见，并为他们的关切采取行动。"

But the ruling reinforces the need for citizens and their elected representatives, not the courts, to ensure equality of access to government. Officials must not be allowed to play favorites in providing information or in arranging meetings simply because an individual or group provides a campaign donation or a personal gift. This type of integrity requires well-enforced laws in government transparency, such as records of official meetings, rules on lobbying, and information about each elected leader's source of wealth.

但该裁决强化了公民和他们选出的代表——而不是法院——来确保平等接触政府的必要性。不得允许官员仅仅因为个人或团体提供了竞选捐款或个人礼物，就在提供信息或安排会议时厚此薄彼。这种诚信需要执行良好的政府透明度法律，如公务会议记录、游说规则，以及每位民选领导人财富来源的信息。

Favoritism in official access can fan public perceptions of corruption. But it is not always corruption. Rather officials must avoid double standards, or different types of access for average people and the wealthy. If connections can be bought, a basic premise of democratic society—that all are equal in treatment by government—is undermined. Good governance rests on an understanding of the inherent worth of each individual.

The court's ruling is a step forward in the struggle against both corruption and official favoritism.

最高法院的裁决是在打击腐败和官方偏袒斗争中迈出的一步。

options.label: A
options.en: The first published sketch, "A Dinner at Poplar Walk" brought tears to Dickens's eyes when he discovered it in the pages of The Monthly Magazine. From then on his sketches, which appeared under the pen name "Boz" in The Evening Chronicle, earned him a modest reputation.
options.zh: 第一篇发表的速写《波普拉散步道之宴》，当狄更斯在《月刊》上发现它时，曾令他热泪盈眶。此后，他以"博兹"为笔名在《晚宪报》上发表的速写，为他赢得了一份不大却实在的声名。

options.label: B
options.en: The runaway success of The Pickwick Papers, as it is generally known today, secured Dickens's fame. There were Pickwick coats and Pickwick cigars, and the plump, spectacled hero, Samuel Pickwick, became a national figure.
options.zh: 正如今天人们所熟知的那样，《匹克威克外传》的一炮而红奠定了狄更斯的名声。市面上出现了匹克威克外套和匹克威克雪茄，而那位肥胖戴镜的主人公塞缪尔·匹克威克成了全国知名人物。

options.label: C
options.en: Soon after Sketches by Boz appeared, a publishing firm approached Dickens to write a story in monthly installments, as a backdrop for a series of woodcuts by the then-famous artist Robert Seymour, who had originated the idea for the story. With characteristic confidence, Dickens successfully insisted that Seymour's pictures illustrate his own story instead. After the first installment, Dickens wrote to the artist and asked him to correct a drawing Dickens felt was not faithful enough to his prose. Seymour made the change, went into his backyard, and expressed his displeasure by committing suicide. Dickens and his publishers simply pressed on with a new artist. The comic novel, The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club, appeared serially in 1836 and 1837, and was first published in book form in 1837.
options.zh: 《博兹速写集》问世后不久，一家出版公司找上狄更斯，请他按月连载一篇故事，作为当时著名画家罗伯特·西摩所创想的一系列木刻的陪衬。狄更斯以一贯的自信，成功坚持要西摩的画来图解他自己的故事。第一期的插图登出后，狄更斯写信给画家，请他修改一幅他觉得不够忠实于自己散文的画。西摩改了画，走进后院，以自杀表达了他的不快。狄更斯和出版商则换了个新画家继续干。这部喜剧小说《匹克威克俱乐部遗稿》于1836和1837年连载，并于1837年首次以书籍形式出版。

options.label: D
options.en: Charles Dickens is probably the best-known and, to many people, the greatest English novelist of the 19th century. A moralist, satirist, and social reformer. Dickens crafted complex plots and striking characters that capture the panorama of English society.
options.zh: 查尔斯·狄更斯很可能是19世纪最知名、对许多人而言也是最伟大的英国小说家。作为道德家、讽刺家和社会改革者，狄更斯构筑了复杂的情节与鲜明的人物，捕捉了英国社会的全景。

options.label: E
options.en: Soon after his father's release from prison, Dickens got a better job as errand boy in law offices. He taught himself shorthand to get an even better job later as a court stenographer and as a reporter in Parliament. At the same time, Dickens, who had a reporter's eye for transcribing the life around him especially anything comic or odd, submitted short sketches to obscure magazines.
options.zh: 父亲出狱后不久，狄更斯谋得一份更好的差事——在律师事务所当跑腿小弟。他自学速记，以便日后谋得更好的工作：法庭书记员和议会记者。与此同时，狄更斯有着记者般善于记录周遭生活（尤其是任何滑稽或古怪之事）的眼光，向一些无名杂志投寄短篇速写。

options.label: F
options.en: Dickens was born in Portsmouth, on England's southern coast. His father was a clerk in the British navy pay office—a respectable position, but with little social status. His paternal grandparents, a steward and a housekeeper possessed even less status, having been servants, and Dickens later concealed their background. Dickens's mother supposedly came from a more respectable family. Yet two years before Dickens's birth, his mother's father was caught stealing and fled to Europe, never to return. The family's increasing poverty forced Dickens out of school at age 12 to work in Warren's Blacking Warehouse, a shoe-polish factory, where the other working boys mocked him as "the young gentleman." His father was then imprisoned for debt. The humiliations of his father's imprisonment and his labor in the blacking factory formed Dickens's greatest wound and became his deepest secret. He could not confide them even to his wife, although they provide the unacknowledged foundation of his fiction.
options.zh: 狄更斯出生于英格兰南部海岸的朴茨茅斯。其父是英国海军薪金处的办事员——地位体面，却少有社会声望。他的祖父母，一位管家与一位女管家，因曾为仆人而身份更低，狄更斯后来隐瞒了他们的背景。狄更斯的母亲据称出自一个更体面的家庭。然而在狄更斯出生前两年，他的外祖父因盗窃被捕并逃往欧洲，再未归来。家境日窘，迫使12岁的狄更斯辍学，到沃伦鞋油厂——一家鞋油工厂——做工，其他童工嘲弄他为"小绅士"。其父随后因债务入狱。父亲入狱的屈辱与在鞋油厂的劳作，构成了狄更斯最大的伤口，也成为他最深的秘密。即便对妻子他也无法吐露，尽管这一切正是其小说不宣的底色。

options.label: G
options.en: After Pickwick, Dickens plunged into a bleaker world. In Oliver Twist, he traces an orphan's progress from the workhouse to the criminal slums of London. Nicholas Nickleby, his next novel, combines the darkness of Oliver Twist with the sunlight of Pickwick. The popularity of these novels consolidated Dickens as a nationally and internationally celebrated man of letters.
options.zh: 继《匹克威克》之后，狄更斯一头扎进了一个更为黯淡的世界。在《雾都孤儿》中，他追述了一个孤儿从济贫院走向伦敦犯罪贫民窟的历程。他的下一部小说《尼古拉斯·尼克尔贝》将《雾都孤儿》的黑暗与《匹克威克》的明快融为一体。这些小说的走红，巩固了狄更斯作为全国乃至国际知名文坛巨匠的地位。
